text:
maria: quick question — noticed dashboard p95 for /v1/complete dropped ~20% after we flipped weighted routing this morning. but when I break down by upstream endpoint the p95s are higher. dashboard p95 looks like a blend that is lower than any single endpoint's p95. is that expected?
kevin: yep saw it too. short answer: it's a sampling/aggregation artifact. when we merge routes we currently compute percentiles on the merged histogram after sampling weights are applied, which can move quantiles in unintuitive ways.
jules: could be worse when sample counts differ a lot between endpoints. the heavier weight stream can dominate median so combined p95 might sit between endpoints but not necessarily equal any.
samir: is this the same thing as when we downsample hot routes and upweight rare ones? I remember a doc that warned about pctl invariance.
kevin: exactly. math explainer: if you have two buckets with different N and different latency distributions, merging pre-quantile vs computing weighted quantile after sampling yields different results. our backend currently merges sampled timers then runs tdigest on the combined stream.
alex-r: proposal: expose a query flag to the API/console: percentile_source = ["raw","per_endpoint","weighted_merge"] and a sample_count threshold to show N/A below X. that would make UX explicit.
maria: I like showing per_endpoint p95 alongside merged p95 and a little tooltip explaining "merged uses routing weights". right now users assume merged is the truth for the route.
jules: +1 on thresholding. for correctness we should also show a confidence band (e.g., 90% CI) for each percentile when counts are low. simple bootstrap or analytic from tdigest would work.
kevin: implementation caveat: computing CI is cheap if we keep histograms, but presenting it in UI needs design. Also we must be careful for rollouts — when we change routing weights mid-window the merged numbers can shift nonlinearly.
ops-bot: deploy noticed: rollout/weighted-routing -> canary 50% @ 1715551200, 100% @ 1715554000
samir: that ops-bot timestamp explains it — weights changed during the dashboard window. so merged p95 shows an average under mixed weights. we should annotate dashboards with rollout events.
alex-r: annotation is good. another idea: add a query param "align_to_rollout" that splits metrics before/after weight change so you can compare p50/p95 for each phase. returns a small timeseries with two points.
maria: UI question: where do we put the per-endpoint breakdown? current design has a flyout. maybe show 3 cols: merged percentile, per-endpoint list (sortable), and sample counts + CI. quick mock:```\nGET /api/metrics?route=/v1/complete&window=1h&percentile=95&percentile_source=per_endpoint\nResponse: {\n  "merged": {"p95":"120ms","count":"45k"},\n  "endpoints": [\n    {"name":"ep-a","p95":"140ms","count":"30k"},\n    {"name":"ep-b","p95":"160ms","count":"8k"}\n  ],\n  "annotations": ["rollout:weighted-routing 50%->100% @1715554000"]\n}\n```
kevin: that example is good. small nit: use numeric values for counts not strings in the real API, but UI layer can stringify. also we should add a "sample_source" meta field (raw_events vs sampled_stream) so users know if numbers are from the full stream or a sampled one.
jules: we should also discuss alerting. SLOs tied to merged p95 could be misleading during rollouts. either alert on both merged and dominant endpoint, or create rollout-aware alerting that evals the worst-affected variant.
samir: +1 on worst-variant alerting. Ops would prefer conservative rules during rollouts.
maria: action items: 1) kevin to add percentile_source param and sample_count threshold API + backend flags (ETA: next sprint). 2) alex-r to mock the UI flyout with CI and rollout annotations (ETA: EOW). 3) ops to make rollout events emit structured annotations (ops-bot already posts but we need perf-annotations)
kevin: I'll sketch the backend patch. rough plan: keep current merge-by-sampled-stream logic as "weighted_merge" default, compute per_endpoint percentiles on stored histos in parallel, and expose CI via tdigest bootstrap. I'll add a query param "rollout_align=true|false" too.
alex-r: will prototype a compact UI: merged p95, per-endpoint table, and an orange flag when sample_count < 1k.
maria: thanks everyone — this should reduce confusion. Samir, can you add a short note to runbook about not relying solely on merged p95 during rollouts?
samir: will do. also will add a checkbox to create alerts against "worst_variant" for any rollout.
kevin: posting demo when I have a PR. in the meantime, for anyone debugging the current spike, use the per-endpoint view and check ops-bot rollout times.
maria: closing loop — will follow up next week on UX mock. :thumbsup:
